newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, Brent/Dubai narrows sharply.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, Brent/Dubai narrows sharply.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Wednesday in Asia with a marked narrowing of the Brent/Dubai market keeping the West-to-East arbitrage wide open.
A steeper backwardation on the Dubai market amid a steady contango on the Brent market, sparked a flattening of the Brent/Dubai.
In afternoon dealilngs, Brent/Dubai for June was valued 18/40 cents per barrel, while July was valued 83/90 cents.
This compared with 60/80 and $1.00/$1.10 in late New York on Tuesday. Traders said the narrower spreads would keep the arbitrage for West African crude imports wide open.
Already, they estimated that China had fixed 4.5 million barrels of first-half June loading West African crudes.
A number of July Brent/Dubai deals were seen in London overnight at $1.03 and $1.05 in July and $1.15 in August, while July/August Dubai traded at +6.5 cents and August/September traded at +5 cents.
In the Middle East market, Oman found firmer prices as a U.S. major released two cargoes from its refining schedule at MPM -10 cents, two cents higher than the previous deal last week.
A separate U.S. major and a large trader were the buyers.
Another Oman deal, done last week before the Oman OSP was released on Tuesday, emerged.
A western trader sold 600,000 barrels to a Japanese trader at Dubai quotes +67 cents.
Tapis values dipped slightly, partly as positions were rolled over into June from balance May, causing the May/June spread to come in to around 15 cents from 20/25 cents.
